messages:
mai: Heads-up: noticed a ~12% p99 latency regression on the INT8 serving lane after yesterday's calibration dataset swap. Opening thread.
lucas: Oof. Is that across all models or a specific family?
mai: Mainly the 13B-family on dedicated pools. Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/perf?run=17632
infra-bot: deploy-bot: deployment 5678 promoted INT8-model v4.2 to prod at 1763216123
ravi: 12% p99 is pretty large — any profiler traces? kernel selection logs?
mai: Quick profiler excerpt attached (paste below). Notice KV cache miss spike and a jump in fallback kernel usage.

```
kernel_choice: int8_cu_blend_v2   count=1245   avg_lat=8.6ms
kernel_choice: fp8_prefetch_v1     count= 342   avg_lat=6.1ms
kv_cache_miss_rate: 0.18 -> 0.42
avg_batch_size: 3.1 -> 2.7
p99_token_latency: 64ms -> 72ms
```

lucas: Hmm kv miss rate doubling + smaller batches. Could be sequence length distribution changed in the new calib set causing more cache churn.
tara: I noticed the new calibration corpus has a heavier-tail of multi-turn chats (avg seq_len +18%). If KV warmup relies on short-prefix patterns, warm cache hits drop and we get more cold-starts.
alesha: Did the calibration change also flip per-channel -> per-tensor quant? That can amplify outlier effects.
mai: Yes — to speed up calibs we switched to per-tensor scaling for the last run. That reduced mem for scales but a few attention/ff layers had huge activation outliers.
ravi: That explains it. Per-tensor makes a single scale for entire tensor, outliers blow up scale and quantization error spikes for most values. Kernel selector maybe decided the int8 path quality was too bad and routed to a slower kernel variant (or a slower fallback path that preserves fidelity), raising latency.
lucas: Can we repro locally by running old-calib vs new-calib with per-channel and per-tensor configs? Also try clipping top percentile during calibration.
mai: I ran a quick A/B yesterday:

```
run A: old_calib + per-channel -> p99 baseline
run B: new_calib + per-tensor -> p99 +12%
run C: new_calib + per-channel -> p99 +3%
```

So per-channel helps but doesn't fully recover.
tara: Suggest clipping top 0.1% of activations per-channel during scale compute. That usually reduces outlier influence without removing rare but important tokens.
alesha: Agreed. Another idea: introduce a tiny per-layer bias offset (robust mean) when computing scales for int8 to reduce sensitivity.
ravi: I'll spin up a test matrix: {old/new calib} x {per-channel/per-tensor} x {clip 0.0/0.1/0.5%} x {batch-window 2ms/5ms/10ms} and run perf-run on the dedicated pool. Can someone add the batch-window tweaks? batching heuristics might be interacting here (smaller effective batch caused by longer sequences).
mai: Attached more profiler dump showing kernel fallback categories and KV stats.

```
kernel_fallbacks: slow_path(quant_fallback)= 8.3% -> 19.7%
kv_evictions_per_min: 12 -> 38
avg_kv_age: 220ms -> 94ms
batch_wait_ms: 3.2 -> 1.8
```

infra-bot: perf-run 8910 completed: int8-old-calib p99 ~ baseline; int8-new-calib still +11% (per-tensor); int8-new-calib per-channel +2%
mai: TL;DR: new calibration corpus increases rare long sequences and activation outliers; per-tensor quant + that corpus pushes several layers to bad scales -> more quant error -> runtime selects slower kernels/fallbacks and KV cache churn increases because longer sequences reduce prefix reuse.
lucas: Plan: revert production calibration dataset immediately, add outlier-trimming step to calibration pipeline (default 0.1% per-channel clip), and keep per-channel as default for 13B family. Also add runtime guard: if kernel selection cost delta > 15% revert to previous kernel variant for 30min while we observe.
tara: +1 :thumbsup:
alesha: I'll open a short RFC for the calibration pipeline changes and include the perf matrix results.
mai: Thanks all — I'll queue rollback and tag infra to run ravi's matrix. Keeping this thread updated.
